issues.title: Configuration generated with inconsistent and non-OS compliant line endings
issues.body:
## Overview

Running under Linux (and potentially Windows as well), when Link creates a `.linkconfig` file, MacOS line endings (`⎕UCS 13`) are used, which causes spurious interaction with other Linux tools, _e.g._

```
$ cat ws/.linkconfig
} },watch: "dir",ID: "4.0.17"},

In fact, however, the final byte is `⎕UCS 10`.
```

Link does respects `⎕UCS 10` line endings just fine at read time, so it might be desirable to also use OS-specific line endings at generation as well.


## Reproduction

```
      ]LINK.Create # nonexistent -watch=dir
Linked: # ← /home/x/devel/com.wilsonb.git/scratchpad/bmp/nonexistent [directory was created]

      ⎕UCS d←⎕NREAD('nonexistent/.linkconfig'⎕NTIE 0) 83 ¯1
{
  LinkVersion: { ID: "4.0.17"},

  Settings: {
    watch: "dir",
  },
}

      10 13⍳d
2 1 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 1 1 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 1 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 1 2 2 2 2 1 2 0

```

Note also the trailing `⎕UCS 10` byte.

## Version Information

```
      ]version
 Dyalog  19.0.50027 64-bit Unicode, BuildID 3dae0625
 OS      Linux 6.13.12 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC 1 x86_64
 Link    4.0.17
 SALT    2.915
 UCMD    2.6
 .NET    .NET 8.0.8
 WS      19.0
 Tatin   (unavailable)
 Cider   (unavailable)
```

issues.title: -preloaded should allow patching since a given cutoff
issues.body:
When using the -preloaded switch, how about allowing it to have an argument to indicate that the workspace is partially preloaded. If, for example, the workspace was saved as of 1/1/2025 you could tell -preloaded to only ignore files that were saved prior to that date. You might use -preloaded=1/1/2025 to indicate this, for instance. But if a few of the files had been last changed since that date, then it would load those files normally.

Another syntax might be -preloaded=* which could indicate using the loaded workspace's own timestamp as the cutoff date, rather than a specific date, and only files changed since the workspace was saved would be loaded as new/changed while the bulk of them would be considered as unchanged from the saved copy of the workspace.

(From Dyalog/link#741)
comments: Yes - I've already been thinking that we should incorporate some of the recent build code we have written for applications into Link itself.
But use internation date format: -preloaded=2025-01-01
Agreed - I wasn't sure which format would be best, since there are so many possibilities. This might be extended to optionally include a time-of-day and/or TZ, too.

issues.title: Support multiple items in a single source file
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
As an functionista, I'd like to bunch bags of lil' functions together in a single source file.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
If you edit something that comes from a multi-file, you see the entire multi-text. Insert a new item and it gets defined and saved as such. Remove an item from a multi-text, it gets deleted and the file updated.

(From Dyalog/link#757)
comments:
This would introduce disproporionate cost for very little gain. It would require overhauling the sync parser while breaking compatibility with plenty of tools and user commands that rely on the strict 1:1 file-to-function mapping.

Also, this solves an organizational problem that APL already addresses natively with Namespaces. They are the correct abstraction for grouping related logic, offering superior scoping and encapsulation compared to file-based bundling.

Finally, the current 1:1 model aligns perfectly with Git workflows, ensuring atomic commits and minimizing merge conflicts. Merging unrelated changes in a single multi-function file causes potentially unnecessary friction in a collaborative development enviromnent.

My conclusion: The added complexity would outweigh the convenience of fewer files.

- Namespaces do not allow grouping without it affecting names.
- People in today's world expect multiple functions in a single file.
- It is convenient to be able to distribute a "workspace" as a single file.
- For those that use the style of bags of very small functions, opening one editor window per function is simply not sustainable.
- The interpreter already supports multiple items in a single file.
- Shell scripts are already multiple items in a single file, and should be 1st class source files too.
- Git handles insertions and deletions from a single file just as well as the addition and removal of a file.

That said, maybe it isn't worth complicating Link at this point. Hopefully, Link-like functionality will soon be an integral part of the interpreter, and it already handles multi-files.

issues.title: Link should optionally bring *.md files (markdown) into the workspace
issues.body:
It became common to store help pages in variables that are saved in *.md files because editing them in the workspace is so easy. For that reaon it would be nice if Link would support them in the same way it supports *.APLA files.

(From Dyalog/link#773)
comments:
We certainly cannot treat .md files as .apla because they don't contain valid array notation. Now, Link _does_ support plain text files — though it needs special double-extensions to tell it what to do with them, e.g. .LF.apla and .vec.apla — but those are intended to make it easier to edit an APL application's constants using 3rd party editors. Clearly, .md files are not that.

This request seems to be purely in order to use the IDE's build-in editor to edit arbitrary files — there's nothing special about .md files here over, say, .txt files — which is out of Link's scope, as it'd only clutter the workspace with unnecessary variables. Nevertheless, we could consider allowing a mapping of file extensions to the built-in ones, so one could e.g. declare .md → .LF.apla, but that'd be a separate issue.

issues.title: Add `-merge` switch: allow links into a non-empty namespace
issues.body:
#472: loading a directory of utilities into `#` with `-flatten` fails when `#` already holds application code. Flattened links can be used to add functions to an existing flat workspace, so a non-empty target is a reasonable use case.

```apl
      ]link.create # /repos/tools -flatten
⎕SE.Link.Create: Cannot link a non-empty namespace to a non-empty directory: # ←→ /repos/tools
      ]link.create # /repos/tools -flatten -source=dir
⎕SE.Link.Create: Destination namespace not empty: #
```

## Proposal

New Boolean option `merge` (`]link.create ... -merge`, `opts.merge←1`), default off. It is a link option like any other: accepted in `.linkconfig`, and shown as `Merge` by `]link.status -extended`.

- Takes effect only when `source` is `dir`. If `source` is `auto`, `merge` resolves it to `dir`: the namespace is never exported to the directory, even an empty one, and a missing directory is an error. With `source=ns` the option is ignored.
- Does not require `flatten`. Without it, subdirectories become namespaces as usual; the typical use is with `flatten`.
- The target may be non-empty. Source files are loaded as usual. **If an item of the same name already exists in the namespace, the file replaces it.** All other items are left alone; they are not exported and are not associated with any file.
- No reconciliation. With `merge`, the check that a non-empty namespace matches the directory is skipped. This also allows re-linking a flattened directory into a namespace that already holds its code, which that comparison does not currently handle for flattened links.
- Still one link per namespace. A second `Create` on the same namespace reports "Already linked".
- Normal write rules apply afterwards. A function fixed in the editor, or added with `]link.add`, is written to the root of the linked directory unless `getFilename` decides otherwise. This includes pre-existing functions that were not associated with a file when the link was created.
- `]link.break` removes the link and leaves the namespace contents in place.

```apl
      ]link.create # /repos/tools -flatten -merge
      NewFn←{⍵}
      ]link.add NewFn              ⍝ → /repos/tools/NewFn.aplf
```

Document the option in the **merge** section of `Link.Create.md`, and the extra extended-status field in `Link.Status.md`.

(From Dyalog/link#780)
comments:
This has deviated from what is actually required. 

The actual requirement is a switch to allow links into non-empty namespace - so scope has been reduced to that.
Not required.

issues.title: `-flatten` reports a false clash between a directory and a same-named file
issues.body:
With `-flatten`, subdirectories never become namespaces, but `U.FixFiles` still gives each directory an APL name before its clash check. A directory and a same-named function or script therefore block the whole link.

## Reproduce

```text
A:  foo.aplf   foo/code.aplf
B:  foo/foo.aplf   bar.aplf
C:  util.apln   util/x.aplf
```

```apl
      ]link.create #.x <A> -flatten -source=dir
⎕SE.Link.Create: Files produce clashing APL names:
 <A>/foo.aplf  ←→  #.x.foo
 <A>/foo/      ←→  #.x.foo
```

B and C fail the same way (`foo/` vs `foo/foo.aplf`; `util.apln` vs `util/`). Without `-flatten`, B links fine and A and C are genuine clashes.

## Expected

| Layout | Names in `#.x` with `-flatten` |
|---|---|
| A | `foo` `code` |
| B | `foo` `bar` |
| C | `util` (script) `x` |

Two *files* defining the same flattened name (`a/Foo.aplf` + `b/Foo.aplf`) must still error.

## Fix

`Utils.apln:1338-1348` (`FixFiles`): exclude directory entries from `allnames` before the clash check when `opts.flatten` is set. Do not simply delete the rows: they also drive per-directory loading and the early load of `quadVars.apln` (`:1395-1421`). Check the `fastLoad` branch (`:1336-1340`, late clash check at `:1446`) and the two "mismatch between unscripted namespaces and directories" checks (`:1403`, `:1423`).

## Tests

Add to `Test/test_flattened.aplf`: A, B, C link with the names above; `a/Foo.aplf` + `b/Foo.aplf` still errors; B still works and A, C still fail without flatten; repeat with `fastLoad`.

(From Dyalog/link#781)

issues.title: `]link.diff` and `]link.resync` see every item as unmatched for `-flatten` links
issues.body:
For a link created with `-flatten`, `U.Diff` reports every workspace item as "Item has no corresponding file" and every file as "File has no corresponding item", even when nothing has changed. So `]link.diff` is useless, `]link.resync -proceed` re-reads and re-writes everything, the startup check in `WSLoaded` always sees a stale link, and `]link.create` after `]link.break` fails with "Destination namespace not empty", because the fix for #230 relies on finding no differences and a flattened link always reports differences.

## Reproduce

```apl
      ]link.create #.T G -flatten -source=dir
      ]link.diff #.T                 ⍝ nothing changed
→ #.T      Item has no corresponding file
→ #.T.Foo  Item has no corresponding file
→ #.T.Goo  Item has no corresponding file
←  G/          File has no corresponding item
←  G/Foo.aplf  File has no corresponding item
←  G/Goo.aplf  File has no corresponding item
```

Without `-flatten` the diff is empty.

issues.title: `-source=dir` refuses a namespace that holds more than the directory
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
`]link.create -source=dir` fails with "Destination namespace not empty" when the target namespace holds items that the directory does not define, even though `source=dir` says the directory is the source. The Usage guide ("Starting a new project") says that when both sides hold different code "you will need to specify the `source` option"; the Link.Create API page says `dir` requires an empty namespace. The code follows the API page. Since #230 the only exception is a namespace whose content is identical to the directory.

One case where this matters: linking a partial checkout of a repository into a workspace that already holds the whole application. Link 2.0 allowed this.

**To Reproduce**
1. A directory `ltest` holding `app/code.aplf`, `foo/code.aplf`, `test/code.aplf`, `utils/code.aplf`, each defining the function named after its directory.
2. `]link.create -flatten # ltest`, then `]link.break #`. The workspace now holds the four functions.
3. Edit `app/code.aplf` (or `⎕EX'app'`; either way the workspace no longer matches the directory).
4. `]link.create -flatten -source=dir # ltest`

**Expected behaviour**
The link is created. Items the directory defines are replaced from their files; items it does not define are left alone.

**Session transcript**
```
      ]link.create -flatten # ltest
Linked: # ←→ "/path/to/ltest"
      ]link.break #
Unlinked: #
      ⍝ edit app/code.aplf
      ]link.create -flatten # ltest
ERRORS ENCOUNTERED: ⎕SE.Link.Create: Cannot link a non-empty namespace to a non-empty directory: # ←→ "ltest"
      ]link.create -flatten -source=dir # ltest
ERRORS ENCOUNTERED: ⎕SE.Link.Create: Destination namespace not empty: #
```

**Desktop**
 - OS: Linux
 - APL version: 21.0 Unicode 64-bit
 - `⎕SE.Link.Version`: 4.2.5

**Additional context**
`Create.aplf` line ~98: the `emptydir⍱emptyns` block requires `U.Diff` to be empty regardless of whether `source` was given explicitly or defaulted from `auto`. Related: #136 (introduced the guard), #230, #472, #782.

(From Dyalog/link#788)

issues.title: Nothing is tied under `watch=ns`, so edits to flattened items are written to the link root
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
`U.FixTie` returns 1 only when `watch` is `both`. With `watch=ns` (the only possibility without .NET) no item is tied to its file. For an untied item in a flattened link `U.DetermineFileName` does not know which subdirectory it came from and writes to the link root, so editing a function in APL creates a new `<name>.aplf` at the root and leaves the original file untouched. `]link.refresh` does not help, since it also fixes without ties.

The restriction dates from #140 (August 2020): at the time, deleting a tied script's file lost its source. After 19.0, `⎕NR` and `⎕SRC` of a tied item survive deletion of the file, so the reason no longer applies.

**To Reproduce**
1. A directory `ltest` holding `app/code.aplf`, `foo/code.aplf`, `test/code.aplf`, `utils/code.aplf`, each defining the function named after its directory.
2. `]link.create -flatten -watch=ns # ltest`
3. Edit `app` in the editor (or `#'app' 'app'⎕SE.Link.Fix 'r←app' 'r←46'`).
4. Look at the directory.

**Expected behaviour**
`app/code.aplf` is updated. Nothing is created at the root.

**Session transcript**
```
      ]link.create -flatten -watch=ns # ltest
Linked: # → "/path/to/ltest"
      4⊃5179⌶'app'                  ⍝ no tie

      #'app' 'app'⎕SE.Link.Fix 'r←app' 'r←46'
      ⊃⎕NINFO⍠1⊢'ltest/*.aplf'
 ltest/app.aplf                     ⍝ new file; app/code.aplf still holds r←42
```

**Desktop**
 - OS: Linux
 - APL version: 21.0 Unicode 64-bit
 - `⎕SE.Link.Version`: 4.2.5

**Additional context**
`Utils.apln`, `FixTie`: `tie←'both'≡link.watch`, from #140 (4a2fdb1), moved into FixTie by #99 (b962cc1). Non-flattened links are not affected because the default path follows the namespace structure. `getFilename` can redirect the write but not suppress it (returning `''` means "use the default").
